category_title: Defiant and disengaged boys who resist standard classroom requirements
minimal_context: The student arrives late to class and is directed to a seat in the back to review rules and take out a book.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please come in and take the empty seat in the back.

STUDENT: (Walks in a few minutes after the bell, looking confident and defiant.)

TUTOR: We are reviewing the classroom rules right now.

STUDENT: (Stands confidently and defiantly, looking like trouble.)

TUTOR: Please sit down and take out a book.

STUDENT: (Remains confident and defiant, looking like trouble and beginning to disrupt the class instead of taking out a book.)

options.A: Model the expected reading behavior for the student by demonstrating how to take out a book and instructing him to do it the same as you.
options.B: Direct the student to a seat in the back where he will not bother other students, and after reviewing the classroom rules, ask him to take out a book.
options.C: Articulate the alternatives the student confronts and the actions taken, using comments such as, 'I see you made the decision to focus here,' or 'How can you change this to a better decision?'
options.D: Talk informally with the student about the books he has read recently, engaging in a brief conversation during the session before asking him to take out a book.
